description: Hi there, looking for fun, dedicated and collaborative people to build a great childrens game
summary:
This game was created for young kids (7-12 yrs) in submission for the Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer. 
The challenge is to help young kids understand through fun that being in space requires strategic use of limited resources. In the game, building and conducting research on the Moon or Mars in real life requires resources like oxygen and electricity especially when battling space elements like solar radiation. Kids learn to choose wisely for survival.
details:
This is a single person educational game that's best played on a desktop web browser. It walks a child through various scenarios in space.

It helps kids learn how to manage resources effectively, build a diverse team, learn real life facts about space, follow directions from Mission Control, think through and make decisions, be rewarded and acknowledged for completing their mission duties, reflect on failures, improve, try again, and think about emotional intelligence and teamwork.

This game was built through Lovable vibe coding software with research done on Chatgpt and Google. As a solo builder on this project, and a millennial, I wanted the game design to be a throwback to old school 80s and early 90s (MS-DOS) games. I developed the creative storyline and designed the process taking inspiration from my childhood 80s computer games.

The information provided was as factually accurate as possible to ensure a proper educational experience, and included the options of having diverse characteristics when building the astronaut crew. I wanted young future astronauts from all backgrounds to be able to see themselves represented in the game regardless of who they are, and did research on real life astronauts who represented differently abled people in space.

I hope that kids finish this game feeling inspired and energised to learn more about space exploration and to one day contribute to our understanding of space.
